top_news.title: "Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelenskyy," claims Trump as Ukraine alleges energy ceasefire violation
top_news.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday (local time) said that Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to reach a deal to end the Russia-Ukraine war more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, while reiterating that both leaders must come together to end the conflict amid questions over alleged violations of the proposed energy ceasefire. Speaking to reporters before he travelled to Ohio for a midterm election campaign rally, Trump said he would examine reports on whether Russia had violated the ceasefire, while stressing that both sides had suffered heavy casualties. "I'm not sure about that, and we'll take a look. But all I know is that Zelensky and Putin have to get together and end that ridiculous war. This month they lost 32,000 people in that war, and it's ridiculous. So they have to get together and get it done," Trump said. Asked about reports of Russian strikes despite the ceasefire, Trump said, "Well, I'll have to look at it and see because there's been violations on both sides." When a reporter pointed out that Russia and Ukraine had not both confirmed an agreement to a ceasefire, Trump responded, "Well, they agreed. You know why? Because I said you agree. That's why. They agreed because I said they agreed. And that thing has to get settled." "The war is a disaster. Did you see the numbers that just came out this month? 32,000 mostly soldiers were killed, young people. 32,000 killed. That war has to be over with," he added. On Zelenskyy's position regarding the energy ceasefire and the absence of a public response from Putin, Trump said he believed both leaders supported the proposal and wanted to reach an agreement. "I think they both support it. I think they want to make a deal, but they don't know how, but we're going to get them to make a deal," Trump said. Asked whether he saw Putin's willingness to negotiate despite continued Russian strikes on Ukraine, Trump said, "I think they're going to make a deal. I think actually Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelensky." Trump also defended his decision to allow Russian diesel supplies amid criticism from Republicans, arguing that the arrangement was intended to benefit the wider international market and that restricting supplies could have far-reaching consequences. "Well, I think these Republicans can't really be serious. We make a lot of oil. We could do a restriction on oil, but the rest of the world would be greatly affected if we do that," Trump said. He added that the United States could impose a cap on diesel supplies and reserve the fuel for domestic consumption, but said such a move would have a significant impact elsewhere. "And it's not really a deal with me, it's a deal for the rest of the world. So anything that could help our farmers, our ranches, I like," Trump said, adding that Zelenskyy should focus on reaching an agreement rather than discussing the issue. Trump's remarks come amid competing claims by Moscow and Kyiv over compliance with the proposed energy ceasefire, with Zelenskyy accusing Russia of continuing attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite the US President's announcement. articles.title: "Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelenskyy," claims Trump as Ukraine alleges energy ceasefire violation
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday (local time) said that Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to reach a deal to end the Russia-Ukraine war more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, while reiterating that both leaders must come together to end the conflict amid questions over alleged violations of the proposed energy ceasefire. Speaking to reporters before he travelled to Ohio for a midterm election campaign rally, Trump said he would examine reports on whether Russia had violated the ceasefire, while stressing that both sides had suffered heavy casualties. "I'm not sure about that, and we'll take a look. But all I know is that Zelensky and Putin have to get together and end that ridiculous war. This month they lost 32,000 people in that war, and it's ridiculous. So they have to get together and get it done," Trump said. Asked about reports of Russian strikes despite the ceasefire, Trump said, "Well, I'll have to look at it and see because there's been violations on both sides." When a reporter pointed out that Russia and Ukraine had not both confirmed an agreement to a ceasefire, Trump responded, "Well, they agreed. You know why? Because I said you agree. That's why. They agreed because I said they agreed. And that thing has to get settled." "The war is a disaster. Did you see the numbers that just came out this month? 32,000 mostly soldiers were killed, young people. 32,000 killed. That war has to be over with," he added. On Zelenskyy's position regarding the energy ceasefire and the absence of a public response from Putin, Trump said he believed both leaders supported the proposal and wanted to reach an agreement. "I think they both support it. I think they want to make a deal, but they don't know how, but we're going to get them to make a deal," Trump said. Asked whether he saw Putin's willingness to negotiate despite continued Russian strikes on Ukraine, Trump said, "I think they're going to make a deal. I think actually Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelensky." Trump also defended his decision to allow Russian diesel supplies amid criticism from Republicans, arguing that the arrangement was intended to benefit the wider international market and that restricting supplies could have far-reaching consequences. "Well, I think these Republicans can't really be serious. We make a lot of oil. We could do a restriction on oil, but the rest of the world would be greatly affected if we do that," Trump said. He added that the United States could impose a cap on diesel supplies and reserve the fuel for domestic consumption, but said such a move would have a significant impact elsewhere. "And it's not really a deal with me, it's a deal for the rest of the world. So anything that could help our farmers, our ranches, I like," Trump said, adding that Zelenskyy should focus on reaching an agreement rather than discussing the issue. Trump's remarks come amid competing claims by Moscow and Kyiv over compliance with the proposed energy ceasefire, with Zelenskyy accusing Russia of continuing attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite the US President's announcement.
